disease_label_per_paper: HSV encephalitis with normal CSF analysis
presentation_summary: 60-year-old Indian man developed moderate-grade fever for five days followed by seizure the next day.
During the next 72 hours he developed worsening neurologic symptoms, aggressive behavior, and multiple seizure episodes.
On admission he was febrile at 38 C, normotensive, mildly tachycardic, with slow mentation, generalized slowed responses to verbal commands, and generalized weakness.
Initial lumbar puncture had normal CSF: WBC 0, RBC 0, protein 18 mg/dL, glucose 57 mg/dL with simultaneous serum glucose 113 mg/dL.
Contrast-enhanced MRI showed bilateral temporal enhancement and FLAIR bilateral medial temporal hyperintensities, right greater than left.
CSF PCR returned positive for HSV-1 DNA 72 hours later; he improved on acyclovir and was discharged without neurologic deficit.
